_meta.role: full configuration: the only delivering cell - System-1 recall selection (via the association graph) is inserted into the model view, and the TAS ordering is configured and recorded
_meta.status: run set for the next round (C0, C1, C2)
_meta.note: The project's own configuration: TAS on, recall selection on (`tier1: s1`, the implemented mode), x first; `xFirst: true` and `deliver: true` come from `cellPolicy('C2')` (packages/core/src/types.ts) and are not repeated here, because a value in this file would silently override the cell. The contrast the registered rule tests is this cell against `C0`, the baseline: `C1` is a second control arm that delivers nothing (see its `_meta.secondControl`), so no effect of this arm can be read from a C1-vs-C2 difference - the model reads the same list in C1 as in C0. What that contrast measures today is the recall lane (selection and its insertion); TAS's ordering reaches the model only once the model-view write-back exists, which is a separate project (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).
_meta.tier1: `recall.tier1` is `s1` here, and it said `embed` until 2026-10-02 - a mode with no implementation, read in the whole codebase by exactly one test, `policy.recall.tier1 !== 'off'` (packages/core/src/assembler.ts). No embedder exists, `source: 'embed'` is never assigned to an edge, and the round's own graph snapshot says which scorers ran: `s1-noul` 1 824 edges, `lexical` 253 976, embed **0**. So the cell named a mechanism it does not use while a reader could only find out by grepping; `s1` is the mode that runs (one batched `noul` call). A literal `embed` is now rejected by `validatePolicy` with its own message rather than treated as "not off" (packages/core/src/config.ts, `LEGACY_TIER1`), and `recall.embedModel` - which nothing reads - is warned about when it is non-empty. The tier-1 *axis* of the design remains unmeasured: implementing the embed mode is what would measure it, and that is a separate project, not a rename.
_meta.planGateRemoved: This file carried `planGate: { on: true, ... }` until 2026-10-02, and round `20261002-2037` is why it no longer does. That round - the one this cell was written for - contains **zero** `plan_gate` records: not in its control plane (6 546 records), not on its tape (2 003 lines), not in its session stream, across 277 steps and 289 tool calls. The gate can be reached in exactly two ways, a numbered or bulleted plan in an assistant message (`extractPlans`) or a `todo/write` session event (`extractTodoEvent`), and that run produced neither: the model wrote prose and reasoning, and the event stream carries no `todo/write` at all. So the arm advertised an ordering step it never ran, in the one cell whose whole purpose is to be the full configuration. The knob is removed rather than given a new path, because adding one would change what C2 *is* mid-study - a new plan source means new System-1 calls, and the C1-vs-C2 comparison the file's own `note` rests on would no longer be between the two cells that were run. Nothing takes over the gate's role: the honest reading of round `20261002-2037` is that C2's ordering half was TAS alone, exactly as in C1, and the difference between the two arms was recall selection. `packages/core/src/types.ts` carries the full decision; the mechanism itself (`packages/core/src/plan-gate.ts`, `packages/dsh-plugin/src/plan-gate-runtime.ts`) is kept and still tested for whichever arm next has a plan source the model actually writes to. Two clauses of that record were overtaken on 2026-10-02 and are corrected here rather than rewritten: the C1-vs-C2 comparison this file's `note` used to rest on is no longer the registration (the contrast is C0 vs C2, and `C1` is a second control that delivers nothing - see `C1.json`'s `_meta.secondControl`), and "the difference between the two arms was recall selection" is true of what reached the model only in the sense that C2's one delivery channel inserts recalled turns: the ordering half reached the model in neither arm, which is why the ordering claim this cell's role names is not measurable until the model-view write-back exists.
_meta.retry: `s1.retryAttempts: 2` is set below per docs/CELLS-RUN.md's setup, and this cell needs it most: C2 makes an order of magnitude more System-1 calls than the other two arms, the shared Laya refuses rather than queues at its admission limit, and a measured round lost 732 of 2 016 calls to `503 server busy` - a refused call falls back to the local lexical scorer, so an unrecovered refusal turns an S1-governed cell into a partly lexical one. The retry waits the server's own `Retry-After` and is answered, and `attempts`/`waitedMs` on the `s1_call` record report how often it was needed; report `judgedPairs / scoredPairs` either way.
_meta.admissionLimit: `s1.admissionLimit: 8` is new, and it is the other half of the same problem `retryAttempts` addresses. A retry is the right answer to *one* refusal; it is the wrong answer to a backend refusing everything, because the retry is one more request inside the same admission window. Round `20261002-2037` measured what that costs: 5 992 `s1_call` records over a 2 219.7 s span - **2.70 requests/second** - of which **3 859 (64.4 %)** were refused with `503 {"detail":"server busy"}`, the refusal rate above a third in every thirty-second bucket of the run, 4 057 of them carrying `attempts: 2` and 4 057 000 ms of `waitedMs` between them, for a yield of `judgedPairs / scoredPairs = 4 152 / 860 672 = 0.48 %`. The local Laya admits 16 concurrent requests and refuses the rest; one cell saturated it by itself, because the upkeep queue drains several events per tick without awaiting its async handler, so several scoring loops were in flight at once. The plugin now caps what this cell may have in flight at this number and opens a circuit breaker after a run of refusals, probing once per cooldown until the backend answers again. A window the gate does not send is **deferred**, not scored lexically: the graph holds its cursor over it, the pair is not counted in `scoredPairs`, and it is counted in `deferredPairs` on the assembly record instead - so `judgedPairs / scoredPairs` stays the share of what was offered that the backend answered, and the omission is a number with a reason rather than a lower coverage nobody can see.
_meta.provider: `s1.provider` below names the lane this cell runs. It is `laya-serve`, the **local** backend at `http://127.0.0.1:8008`, and the live per-cell profile pins `s1.baseUrl` to that address (docs/CELLS-RUN.md's setup) - so the value here has to be the one the profile overrides it with, or the file describes a lane no cell uses. It previously read `jev`, the earlier **remote** System-1 service, which is not what any run has used and which would additionally have needed an API key it does not have: a reader who took that value seriously would look for a credential that nothing requires. What a cell actually ran is recorded, and can be re-read, from its own `kind:"wiring"` tape record - `verify-wiring.mjs` asserts it - so treat that record, not this file, as the authority.
